Suppose we use a spreadsheet to randomly generate maths marks for students, and separately generate random English marks.
PMCC between Maths and English marks in this first set of data?
But what is the true underlying PMCC between Maths and English?

0. It was stated above that the maths and English marks were generated independently of each other. Independent variables, by definition, have no correlation. The observed PMCC may vary from the true PMCC because the data is randomly sampled, just as if we threw a fair die, we wouldn’t necessarily see equal counts of each outcome.
(i.e. English/Maths marks have no underlying correlation), the observed PMCC for the sample,
, could vary, and might, purely by chance, suggest some correlation. In the first sample, this happened to be positive, in the latter, negative.
If we increased the sample size (in this case 10), we’d expect the observed PMCC to more closely match the true PMCC (0).
